title: Board of Governors closed for Veterans Day (observed) while the NYSE, the Reserve Banks and the bond market all trade a full session — and the date is D+3 of the 2028 presidential election
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm, 'K.8 - Holidays Observed by the Federal Reserve System 2026-2030', re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: July 8, 2026'). Its header states the rule verbatim -- 'For holidays falling on Saturday, Federal Reserve Banks and Branches will be open the preceding Friday; however, the Board of Governors will be closed' -- and its first footnote names this exact date without inference: 'Saturday - the Federal Reserve Banks are open, but the Board of Governors is closed on July 3, 2026, June 18, 2027, December 24, 2027, December 31, 2027, and November 10, 2028.' The 2028 column reads Veterans Day 'November 11*' against that footnote, and 2028-11-11 is a Saturday (computed, not assumed). The equity side is primary-sourced the other way: nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes), states 'All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028' and its ten-row table carries NO Veterans Day row in any year, with the only 2028 early closes named as Monday July 3 and Friday November 24. The bond side is now primary-sourced too (the gap the sibling entry could not close): sifma.org's own US Holiday Archive, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 338,642 bytes), records Veterans Day as 'None' in 2017 and as an empty cell in 2023 -- the two prior Saturday-Veterans-Day years -- against 'Friday, November 11' full closes in 2016 and 2022; corroborated by home.treasury.gov's daily par yield curve, which carries a full curve on 2000-11-10, 2006-11-10, 2017-11-10 and 2023-11-10 (4 of 4) and NO row on 2005-11-11, 2011-11-11, 2016-11-11 or 2022-11-11 (0 of 4). Held estimate on the same two counts as its sibling fed-board-closure-2027-12-31: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an agency's own internal holiday schedule as distinct from a market calendar. The DATE is not in doubt -- the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own initial research (2026-09-09), after reading the sole prior proposal, `fed-board-closure-2028-11-10.from-fed-board-closure-2027-12-31.json`, which is now inert. The proposal's two open gaps are BOTH CLOSED and its framing is AMENDED. (1) THE BOND SIDE TRADES. SIFMA's own archive records Veterans Day as 'None' in 2017 and blank in 2023 -- when the holiday falls on a Saturday there is no fixed-income closure and no early close, unlike Saturday Independence Day (2020-07-03) and Saturday Christmas (2021-12-24), which SIFMA does roll onto the preceding Friday. Treasury's par yield curve agrees 4-of-4 open against 0-of-4 on Veterans-Day-on-a-Friday. (2) THE EXPIRATION QUESTION IS ANSWERED BY COMPUTATION, not by the OCC file, whose data rows genuinely stop at 2027-12-31 (155 rows, 2025-01-01 onward, re-fetched 2026-09-09): November 2028's monthly equity/index expiration is 2028-11-17 (third Friday) and the monthly volatility-products expiration is 2028-11-15 (the Wednesday 30 days before the 2028-12-15 third Friday). Nothing monthly expires on 2028-11-10. (3) THE OUT-OF-SAMPLE TEST THE PROPOSAL ASKED FOR REPLICATES: on the Board's own release archive, H.8 is 404 on all four reachable Saturday-Veterans-Day Fridays (2000/2006/2017/2023-11-10) against 8-of-8 matched ordinary-November-Friday controls at 200, and H.4.1 is 200 on all four preceding Thursdays and 404 on all four Fridays. 2028-11-09 is a Thursday, so the balance sheet lands as normal. (4) THE PROPOSAL'S 'CLEANER MEMBER OF THE CLASS' FRAMING IS THE ONE THING THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE, and it is corrected here: 2028-11-10 is not a context-free Friday. Because Nov 11 falls on a Saturday exactly when Nov 7 is the Tuesday after the first Monday, EVERY instance of this configuration is D+3 of a US general election -- all seven since 1978, by identity rather than coincidence -- and 2028 is a PRESIDENTIAL year. The set's one large move, 2000-11-10 at -2.44%, is the disputed Bush-v-Gore recount week. The election is proposed in the same PR as `proposals/presidential-election-2028-11-07.from-fed-board-closure-2028-11-10.json`; it is the dominant adjacency and this calendar did not carry it. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED: symbols is empty, no house playbook is calendar-keyed, and the impact tier stays low because the closure itself displaces one low-impact weekly statistical release and nothing the market prices. Estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
